7g2eh1pk89rnko1uv98il5221t.value: Credits: the spacetime algebra, with boosts as rotors, the spacetime split into relative vectors σₖ = γₖγ₀, the field as one bivector F = E + IB and a charge's motion in a constant field as u(τ) = e^(τF/2) u₀ e^(−τF/2), is David Hestenes' (Space-Time Algebra, 1966; New Foundations for Classical Mechanics, 1986), as presented by Chris Doran and Anthony Lasenby (Geometric Algebra for Physicists, 2003) (prior art). Relativistic velocity addition is Einstein's (1905) and the transformed fields are Lorentz's and Einstein's; here they come out of the rotor product rather than being written in. The page and its layout are ours.

ukefbegeaihugpfnicqikmb4fg.value: Spacetime: relativity and electromagnetism as rotors

no1q2dl2evlmjj4v6bjtqm9m94.value: Everything here is a product in one algebra, Cl(1, 3), the spacetime algebra. A boost is a rotor, so two boosts make one by multiplying, and relativistic velocity addition falls out. The electromagnetic field is one bivector, F = E + I B; a moving observer sees R̃ F R; and a charge in the field moves by the rotor e^(τF/2).

p0nbudoag8aiiouph0iagpvcl0.value: The middle row is R₂R₁ γ₀ (R₂R₁)~, read off; the formula under it is only there to compare.

j9oohbrhvornr7bgam97onmt0j.value: The field a moving observer sees

jgthadmp0uus67se2vmc8as4uu.value: F′ = R̃ F R with R the boost by β₁ along x. E′ and B′ are read off as ⟨F′σ₂⟩ and the I part of F′σ₃. F² = E² − B² + 2I E·B is the same for every observer.

29hhuuog5kqbr7n8h8ksr7u5iq.value: B > E: F² < 0, the step rotor is a rotation. The charge loops and drifts along E × B, here along x.

139igkvt1g8c030eirs0ct29lm.value: E > B: F² > 0, the step rotor is a boost. No frame sees a pure magnetic field, and the charge runs away faster and faster.

823nepm82fjduh1io2tq7sccpb.value: E = B: F² = 0, the step rotor is 1 + dτF/2. The charge is swept along x ever faster.

6jt6mg007ag9n6hb4e2rpfu5b6.value: Starts at rest where the axes cross; 400 proper-time steps of 0.06, charge over mass 1, c = 1. Change E and B on the card beside this one.

p4iiuqbvcju8smtvc9r385dnoj.value: Why this works: the boost by β along x is e^(φ/2 σ₁) with tanh φ = β, and two boosts along the same line multiply to e^((φ₁ + φ₂)/2 σ₁), so rapidities add and speeds combine by tanh(φ₁ + φ₂). The field's square is E² − B² + 2I E·B, which a rotor sandwich can't change, so those two numbers are invariants. And because F² is a number when E and B are at right angles, clifford exp can make the rotor for the charge's motion in one step.

g2nps63npmgi6fg7lcep0vfrlp.value: Here E points along y and B along z only. With E·B ≠ 0, F² has an I part, and clifford exp, which needs a bivector whose square is a number, can't exponentiate it (yet).
